issues.legal_issue: A seller cannot enforce a construction deadline found only in an allotment letter, or demand an additional price for delayed construction, after conveying absolute ownership by a registered sale deed that contains no such condition.
material_facts: The purchasers paid the full consideration for the industrial plots, and the seller executed registered sale deeds in their favour.
The deadline for implementing the project appeared in the allotment letters, but not in the sale deeds or the sale agreements.
The seller issued cancellation notices years after the sale deeds were executed, when the purchasers had not constructed their units; the purchasers said basic infrastructure had not been provided.
The seller later withdrew the cancellation action and offered another opportunity to construct subject to payment of 50% of the prevailing market value.
issues.conclusion: The allotment-letter deadline ceased to be enforceable after the absolute registered conveyances because it was not included as a condition in the sale deeds. The seller could not cancel the conveyances or demand the additional market-value payment; the demand had no legal basis.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 5, 8, 10, 11 and 55 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, an absolute transfer passes the transferor’s interest, and a direction repugnant to an interest created absolutely is generally ineffective. After the buyer performs the obligations and the seller conveys ownership, the seller cannot unilaterally cancel the conveyance. Indu Kakkar v. Haryana State Industrial Development Corporation Ltd. (1999) 2 SCC 37 does not govern where, unlike there, the conveyance contains no condition super-added to the transfer. The Court also referred to the Transfer of Property Act, the Indian Contract Act, 1872, and the Specific Relief Act, 1963, as governing the parties’ rights after execution of the sale deed.

predicates.civil_appeal_from_writ_decision: The matter is an appeal from a decision in writ proceedings concerning a public authority’s action.
predicates.registered_absolute_transfer: The seller conveyed absolute ownership to the buyer through a registered instrument after receiving the agreed consideration.
predicates.deadline_only_in_pre_sale_document: A construction deadline appeared in a preliminary allotment document but was not included as a condition in the final conveyance.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a writ decision concerns a registered absolute transfer and the deadline appeared only in a preliminary document, the seller cannot cancel the transfer or demand an extra price.

issues.legal_issue: A public authority cannot justify a challenged administrative order by relying on a ground that was not stated as a basis for the order and was not supported by the case pleaded or the record.
material_facts: The stated basis for cancellation and the later additional-payment demand was the failure to establish units within the specified time.
The seller argued during the appeals that some purchasers had used or intended to use the land for a purpose other than building a factory.
That alleged misuse had not been pleaded in the High Court, was not the stated basis for cancellation or the payment demand, and was unsupported by material on the record.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the new-purpose argument and held that the challenged action had to be assessed on the reasons originally given, not on a new ground advanced later.
issues.legal_principle: In Mohinder Singh Gill v. Chief Election Commissioner, (1978) 1 SCC 405, relying on Commissioner of Police, Bombay v. Gordhandas Bhanji, AIR 1952 SC 16, the Court held that an order made on stated grounds must be judged by those grounds and cannot be validated by fresh reasons later supplied. A public order is construed objectively by reference to its language.

predicates.appeal_challenging_public_authority_orde: The proceeding is an appeal challenging an order made by a public authority.
predicates.later_ground_not_stated_in_order: A ground relied on during the appeal was not stated as a basis for the challenged order.
predicates.later_ground_not_supported_by_record: The later ground was not pleaded or supported by material in the record.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a public authority’s order and a later, unsupported ground was not stated in that order, that ground cannot support the order.
